items.review_rationale: Read the topological separated-map criterion through its diagonal into a fibre product of spaces, with a closed image requirement. Avoided conflating this with separated morphisms of schemes or with Hausdorffness of every topology.

references.context: Subspace of X×X consisting of pairs (x_1,x_2) with equal f-images, carrying the pullback/subspace topology
Map x↦(x,x), well-defined since both projections to Y equal f(x)
Diagonal subset is closed in the pullback topological space, not merely closed in X×X unless additional target assumptions hold

references.disposition: This is a topological map property and is not identified with closed-immersion of a scheme diagonal.

items.review_rationale: Read the cofinality condition for an ordinary functor H:I→J through the comma category (j↓H), including its object arrows j→H(i), nonemptiness and zigzag connectedness. Preserved arrow orientation and distinguished cofinality from cofinal subset of a well-order.

references.context: Category with objects (i,j→H(i)) and morphisms in I commuting with the structure arrows out of j
Objects of the under-comma construction, oriented from fixed j toward values of H

references.phrase: for every object j of J
references.disposition: The comma category must be nonempty and connected at each j, not merely at some objects.

items.review_rationale: Read initiality using the opposite-oriented comma category (H↓j) with arrows H(i)→j for every target j; retained the connectedness requirement and contrasted this explicitly with the cofinal-functor direction.

references.context: Category whose objects are arrows H(i)→j with compatibility-preserving arrows from I
Objects of the over-comma construction, oriented toward fixed target j rather than away from it

references.phrase: nonempty and connected for all j
references.disposition: Universal quantification over the objects of J is required; one connected comma category does not suffice.

items.review_rationale: Read nth roots of unity as solutions of ζ^n=1 in a field and separately the assertion that all solutions form a multiplicative subgroup of F×; distinguished arbitrary roots from primitive roots of exact order n.

references.phrase: multiplicative group F× of field units
references.context: The nonzero elements of F under field multiplication, with inverses and identity 1
The product of n copies of ζ in F equals the multiplicative identity 1_F

references.phrase: all nth roots form a subgroup
references.disposition: Closure under products and inverses follows from field commutativity; primitiveness is not required.
